blogs.title: The High Bar of Harm: The Tenth Circuit’s Strict Interpretation of 'Persecution'
blogs.description: This post analyzes the court's decision that death threats and psychological trauma—including a child's panic attacks and a parent's insomnia—do not constitute 'persecution' without accompanying physical violence. It explores the tension between the legal definition of persecution and the lived reality of applicants facing severe coercion and threats of death.

blogs.title: Political Opinion or Personal Vendetta? Deciphering the 'Central Reason' Nexus
blogs.description: Focusing on the 'nexus' requirement, this post examines how the court distinguished between the petitioners' political activism and their professional dispute with a narco-trafficker. It discusses the 'central reason' vs. 'tangential' distinction in mixed-motive cases and the evidentiary burden on claimants to prove that a protected ground was the primary motivator for harm.

blogs.title: The Reporting Paradox: Proving Government Inaction in Jimenez v. Bondi
blogs.description: This post critiques the court's reasoning regarding the 'unable or unwilling' standard. It analyzes the paradox where asylum seekers are expected to report threats to a government they claim is corrupt or complicit in order to prove that the government is unable to protect them, and how the Tenth Circuit viewed a 'one-off conversation' with an unhelpful officer.

blogs.title: Safe Havens or Danger Zones? The Feasibility of Internal Relocation
blogs.description: This post discusses the legal standard for internal relocation within a home country. It evaluates the court's conclusion that relocating within Colombia was reasonable, considering the tension between localized threats (neighborhood-specific) and the broad reach of narco-trafficking organizations with ties to the national presidency.
